prompt:
The batch cannot go to the customer until the sintered part has been checked at both ends, so the process engineer sets a micrometer on each end of one compact and photographs the bench as it stands.

A sintered cylindrical compact lies on the inspection bench with a digital micrometer clamped on each end face. The frames are lettered: N stands on the end that took the top punch, F on the end away from it. The process card propped against the part gives the die bore as 20.00 millimetres, the powder grade as FC-0208, and the press as single action from the top punch. The same card carries the shrink figures for this grade: on sintering the dense end of a compact draws in by 1.2 per cent and the loose end by 0.4 per cent. Behind the bench stand the press and a row of sintering boats.

Which figure each micrometer settles on is what the process card does not give.
easy_question: Does this picture show a sintered cylindrical part lying on an inspection bench with a digital micrometer clamped on each of its end faces? Answer yes or no only.

steps.ask: Read the figure showing on the display of the micrometer whose frame is lettered F, and give it in millimetres.
Read the figure showing on the display of the micrometer whose frame is lettered N, and give it in millimetres.
